title: String Functions
story: You're building a text messaging app. Users want to SHOUT, whisper, and count characters. You need a set of text-transformation tools!
why: Text is everywhere in programs — names, messages, passwords. String functions let you transform, measure, and manipulate text programmatically.
analogy: String functions are like a text factory conveyor belt — raw text goes in one end, and transformed text comes out the other.
try_it: Write an `exclaim` function that takes text and returns it with three exclamation marks added. Then write `whisper_exclaim` that whisper-fies it first, then adds the exclamation marks.
tips: `string.str_upper()` and `string.str_lower()` return NEW strings — they don't change the original
`string.str_len()` counts EVERY character: letters, spaces, punctuation, and numbers
Chain string operations by calling one function inside another: `string.str_upper(whisper(text))`
common_mistakes: Writing `str_upper` without `string.` — the full name is `string.str_upper(text)`
Expecting the original variable to change — `string.str_upper(name)` returns a new string, leaving `name` unchanged
Using string.len() instead of string.str_len() — different languages use different names
